evals.query: I have a Kora 2.0 Java service. Enable declarative method logging from scratch — what dependencies, processor and module do I need?
expected_behavior: Adds implementation "io.koraframework:logging-logback" versioned through the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform (koraVersion=2.0.0.RC2), without pinning a version on the individual artifact
Adds the mandatory annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors", which contains logging-annotation-processor
Extends io.koraframework.logging.logback.LogbackModule on the @KoraApp interface (it extends LoggingModule, which supplies the ILoggerFactory and the LoggingLevelApplier)
Uses io.koraframework.logging.common.annotation.Log on a non-final class and method
Does NOT add declarative-logging-annotation-processor — that is a Kora 1.x artifact and is not in the 2.0 BOM
Does not use the ru.tinkoff.kora group, the kora-parent BOM, or ru.tinkoff.kora.* imports

evals.query: Same thing for my Kotlin Kora 2.0 service — how do I wire up @Log with KSP?
expected_behavior: Adds ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors:${property("koraVersion")}") — the ksp configuration does not inherit the BOM platform, so it carries the version
Adds implementation("io.koraframework:logging-logback") and the kora-bom platform
Extends LogbackModule on the @KoraApp interface
Marks the class and the annotated function open, because the aspect is a generated subclass
Does NOT add declarative-logging-symbol-processor — a Kora 1.x artifact absent from the 2.0 BOM
Does not reference ru.tinkoff.kora or kora-parent

evals.query: My Kotlin build fails with "AOP aspect cannot be applied to class 'com.example.OrderService' because the class is not open" after I added @Log. What is going on?
expected_behavior: Explains that the Kora aspect is woven into a generated $OrderService__AopProxy subclass, so the target must be extensible
Marks both the class and the annotated function open
Notes the class must not be abstract, and that top-level functions cannot be woven at all
States that Kora 2.0 reports this as an explicit compile error rather than skipping the aspect silently
Does not suggest disabling the processor, adding all-open plugins as the primary fix, or switching to a hand-written SLF4J logger

evals.query: In Java I put @Log on a method of a final service class and the build now fails. Why can't Kora just log it?
expected_behavior: Explains the subclass proxy requirement: neither the class nor the annotated method may be final, and the class needs a public, protected or package-private constructor
Quotes or paraphrases the compile error "AOP aspect cannot be applied to class ... because the class is final"
Removes final from the class (and the method if it is final)
Adds that self-invocation via this.method() and objects built with new bypass the aspect for the same reason
Does not claim the aspect is silently skipped
Corrects the key to logging.levels (plural) — LoggingConfig exposes Map<String, String> levels(); logging.level is an unknown key that is ignored without a warning
Quotes the dotted logger name, e.g. "com.example.OrderService": "DEBUG", because an unquoted dotted key nests into HOCON objects and matches no logger
Explains that the argument payload is gated on the more verbose of DEBUG and the entry level, so at INFO only the bare > and < markers appear
Mentions that the logger is named <fully-qualified class>.<method>, so a level on the class covers all its method loggers
Does not tell the user to edit per-logger levels in logback.xml as the fix

evals.query: My logback.xml has <logger name="com.example" level="DEBUG"/> and <root level="WARN"/>, but at runtime everything logs at INFO and my @Log data never appears. What resets it?
expected_behavior: Identifies LoggingLevelRefresher: it is a @Root Lifecycle whose init() calls LoggingLevelApplier.reset(), setting ROOT to INFO and clearing every other logger's level, and only then applies logging.levels
Concludes that per-logger levels in logback.xml do not survive graph initialisation
Moves both the ROOT level and the per-package level into the logging.levels map in application.conf, with quoted keys
Keeps logback.xml for appenders and encoders only
Does not suggest removing LogbackModule or LoggingModule to keep logback.xml levels

evals.query: I set httpServer.telemetry.logging.enabled = true in application.conf but my service method annotated with @Log still logs nothing useful. Are these the same setting?
expected_behavior: States clearly that they are different switches: <component>.telemetry.logging.enabled controls Kora's built-in component telemetry (httpServer, httpClient, jdbc, kafka) and defaults to false in TelemetryConfig.LoggingConfig
States that the @Log aspect is independent of it and is governed by the annotation plus the SLF4J logger level from logging.levels
Directs the user to raise the <class> or <class>.<method> logger to DEBUG in logging.levels to see argument and result payloads
Does not claim that telemetry.logging.enabled turns @Log on or off

evals.query: Porting a Kora 1.x service: we used to stash a correlationId in the Kora Context and read it back in an interceptor for logging. How do I do that in Kora 2.0?
expected_behavior: States that the Kora Context type has been removed from the entire framework in 2.0 and has no drop-in replacement, so the 1.x code must be rewritten rather than repackaged
Points to io.koraframework.logging.common.MDC, held in a ScopedValue<MDC> (MDC.VALUE), as the 2.0 store for per-call logging context
Uses @Mdc on the method or parameter, or MDC.put/MDC.remove imperatively, instead of Context

Notes that a ScopedValue binding is not inherited by threads you start yourself, and that Kora binds the scope at its entry points (Undertow handler, Kafka record handlers, gRPC transport filter, JMS listener, JDK/Quartz jobs)
Does not import ru.tinkoff.kora.common.Context or invent an io.koraframework Context type

evals.query: A plain JUnit test that calls my @Mdc-annotated service method throws java.util.NoSuchElementException from MDC.get(). The same method works fine when called through the HTTP endpoint.
expected_behavior: Explains that Kora's MDC lives in a ScopedValue (MDC.VALUE) and that reading an unbound ScopedValue throws NoSuchElementException
Notes the @Mdc aspect's first generated statement is MDC.get().values(), so it needs a binding, while Kora entry points establish one per request/record/job
Wraps the call in ScopedValue.where(MDC.VALUE, new MDC()).run(...) / .call(...) for the test
Does not suggest switching to org.slf4j.MDC or removing @Mdc to make the test pass

evals.query: I put @Log.off on internalCleanup() to silence it and @Log.result on computeTotal() to log its return value, but internalCleanup still logs and computeTotal logs nothing at all.
expected_behavior: Explains that only @Log, @Log.in and @Log.out weave the aspect (they are @AopAnnotation); @Log.result and @Log.off are @AopPropagate modifiers
States @Log.result alone logs nothing — it needs @Log or @Log.out on the same method, where it only sets the level of the out payload
States @Log.off on a method does not silence it — with @Log.out it still emits the < record and only drops the out payload; to silence a method remove its @Log* annotations
Keeps @Log.off on parameters as the way to omit a single argument
Does not invent a Level.OFF or a @Log(enabled = false) attribute

evals.query: Set the @Log level on debugOperation to DEBUG in my Kora 2.0 Java service.
expected_behavior: Writes @Log(Level.DEBUG) — the level is the annotation's value attribute, typed org.slf4j.event.Level; @Log(level = ...) does not compile
Imports org.slf4j.event.Level
Notes org.slf4j.event.Level has only TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR — there is no Level.OFF
Mentions that arguments are emitted at max(their own level, the entry level) with a DEBUG floor
Does not put @Log on the class — @Log targets METHOD and PARAMETER only

evals.query: In Kotlin, @Log.in doesn't compile on my service function. How do I log only the method entry?
expected_behavior: Writes the annotation with backticks: @Log.`in` — in is a Kotlin keyword
Keeps the class and the function open
Notes @Log.out, @Log.result and @Log.off need no backticks
Warns not to also put a level on @Log: when both @Log(A) and @Log.`in`(B) are present Kotlin uses A while Java uses B
Does not suggest importing an aliased annotation or falling back to a manual logger

evals.query: authenticate(username, password, refreshToken) should log the username but never the password or the refresh token.
expected_behavior: Annotates the method with @Log from io.koraframework.logging.common.annotation
Adds @Log.off to the password and refreshToken parameters, which removes them before any mapper is consulted so they are never rendered at any level
Optionally adds @Mdc(key = "user") to username for context
Mentions @Mask as the alternative when the object must still be logged with only some fields redacted
Does not log secrets through toString(), a manual logger call, or by relying on the logger level alone

evals.query: In my Kotlin Kora 2.0 service I log a User object with @Log. Its Credentials.token must appear redacted rather than disappear. How?
expected_behavior: Annotates the logged types with @Json and @Mask, and the sensitive property with @Mask (optionally @Mask(MaskingKeepLast::class))
Annotates the logged parameter with both @Mask and @Json so the payload is a nested JSON object rather than one escaped string
Explains that KSP generates a $User_MaskingRulesModule @Module supplying MaskingRules<User>, and that generated @Module interfaces must NOT be added to the @KoraApp extends clause
Requires io.koraframework.json.common.JsonModule in the @KoraApp so a JsonWriter<User> exists
Mentions the built-in strategies MaskingFull, MaskingKeepFirst and MaskingKeepLast bound as @DefaultComponent by LoggingModule
Does not use @Log.off, which would remove the value entirely instead of redacting it

evals.query: I did the same @Mask setup in Java on Kora 2.0.0.RC1 and the build now fails resolving io.koraframework.logging.common.masking.MaskingRules<User>. What's missing, and what changes on RC2?
expected_behavior: Identifies that in RC1 logging-annotation-processor had no META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor entry, so javac never ran the processor that generates $User_MaskingRulesModule

Says 2.0.0.RC2 (#921) registers LoggingAnnotationProcessor (isolating since #970), so Java generates $User_MaskingRulesModule like KSP does and the fix is upgrading, keeping annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Offers a hand-written MaskingRules<User> @Module (MaskingRules.builder(User.class).mask(path, strategy).build()) only as the RC1 stop-gap, to be deleted after the upgrade
Warns that a leftover hand-written MaskingRules<User> overrides the generated @DefaultComponent and ignores later @Mask edits
Keeps @Mask (+ @Json) on the logged parameter so the aspect still selects MaskedStructuredArgumentMapper
Does not suggest adding declarative-logging-annotation-processor or forcing -processor on javac

evals.query: On createOrder in my Kotlin service, add MDC keys for the tenant taken from the tenantId parameter and a generated requestId UUID.
expected_behavior: Adds a parameter-level @Mdc(key = "tenant") to tenantId, where the argument itself is the value

Adds a method-level @Mdc(key = "requestId", value = "\${java.util.UUID.randomUUID().toString()}") — the ${...} body is inlined into the generated code, and in Kotlin the $ must be escaped so the string template does not consume it
States that a method-level @Mdc requires both key and value, otherwise the processor fails with "@Mdc annotation must have 'key'/'value' attribute"
Relies on @Mdc being @Repeatable rather than inventing a container attribute
Notes non-global keys are captured and restored in a finally block, so they cannot leak to the caller
Does not call org.slf4j.MDC.put in the function body

evals.query: Porting a Kora 1.x service: can I keep @Mdc and @Log on my methods that return CompletionStage or Mono?
expected_behavior: States that @Mdc fails the build for Publisher (Mono/Flux), Future and CompletionStage return types, e.g. "@Mdc can't be applied for type java.util.concurrent.CompletionStage"
States that the Java @Log aspect rejects Publisher and Future returns at compile time
Explains that Kora 2.0 contracts are synchronous on virtual threads, so the method should be rewritten to return the value directly
Ties the @Mdc restriction to the ScopedValue model: the MDC binding ends with its scope, so a value completed elsewhere would escape it
Does not suggest adding reactor-core or restoring async signatures to keep the annotations

evals.query: Our Kora 2.0 HTTP server logs request bodies at TRACE and I can see passwords and card numbers in the JSON bodies. I already use @Mask on my DTOs. How do I mask the logged bodies, keeping the last four digits of card.number?
expected_behavior: Explains that @Mask / MaskingRules only apply to structured arguments such as @Log payloads, not to transport telemetry bodies, and that no DataMasker is registered by default

Registers a io.koraframework.logging.common.masking.raw.DataMasker component tagged @Tag(io.koraframework.http.server.common.telemetry.HttpServerTelemetry.class), built as new JsonDataMasker(MaskingPathRules.builder().mask("password", new MaskingFull()).mask("card.number", new MaskingKeepLast()).build())

Explains the HTTP body converter picks the masker by format() from the Content-Type (json for */json and *+json, xml for */xml and *+xml, form-urlencoded for application/x-www-form-urlencoded), so a FormUrlencodedDataMasker or XmlDataMasker is needed for those bodies
Explains rule syntax: a bare name matches at any depth, a dotted path is anchored at the payload root, * matches one segment, array elements add no segment; names match case-insensitively
Mentions fail-closed behaviour: a payload the scanner cannot parse is replaced from that point by <masked:unparseable>, and output is capped at 64 KiB by default with <masked:truncated>
Notes the masker is only seen by the transport whose tag it carries (HttpClientTelemetry for the client side)
anti_behavior: Claims @Mask on the DTO masks HTTP telemetry bodies
Invents a config key such as telemetry.logging.maskBody or mask

evals.query: Kora has @Mask, MaskingRules, DataMasker, maskHeaders and a JSON encoder maskField. Which one masks what, and how do they relate?
expected_behavior: Describes @Mask / MaskingRules<T> as masking fields of a typed object while its JsonWriter writes a structured argument (@Log arguments and results)

Describes DataMasker (JsonDataMasker, XmlDataMasker, FormUrlencodedDataMasker) as a fail-closed soft parser over raw payload bytes, used for HTTP server/client bodies and Kafka consumer key/value, registered per transport by @Tag of its telemetry class

Describes maskHeaders / maskQueries as config name lists whose values are replaced by a MaskingStrategy tagged with the transport's telemetry class, defaulting to "***" — and that there is no mask config key
Describes <maskField> as a JsonRecordEncoder-only, field-name match on the final JSON record that cannot see inside string values
States the shared pieces: MaskingRules extends MaskingPathRules (same rule syntax) and all layers use the MaskingStrategy interface
anti_behavior: Presents the layers as alternatives that cover the same input
